ontology_metadata.name: Breast Cancer Misinformation Ontology
ontology_metadata.description: A compact, purpose-built ontology for detecting misinformation in breast cancer patient conversations. Combines concepts from NCI Thesaurus, UMLS, MedQuAD Cancer.gov, and clinical guidelines.
sources: MedQuAD Cancer.gov QA pairs (Ben Abacha & Demner-Fushman, 2019)
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer

BreastCancerSubtype.description: Histological and molecular subtypes of breast cancer

instances.name: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
instances.description: Most common type (~70-80% of breast cancers), begins in milk duct lining

instances.name: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma
instances.description: Second most common type (~10-15%), begins in milk-producing lobules

instances.name: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
instances.description: Non-invasive; abnormal cells in duct lining have not spread. Stage 0.

instances.name: Lobular Carcinoma In Situ
instances.description: Abnormal cells in lobules; increases risk but seldom becomes invasive

instances.name: Inflammatory Breast Cancer
instances.description: Rare, aggressive; breast is warm, red, swollen. Cancer cells block lymph vessels.

instances.name: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
instances.description: ER-negative, PR-negative, HER2-negative. No targeted hormone/HER2 therapy available.

instances.name: HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
instances.description: Overexpresses HER2 protein. Responds to HER2-targeted therapies.

instances.name: Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer
instances.description: ER-positive and/or PR-positive. Responds to endocrine therapy.

instances.name: Paget Disease of the Nipple
instances.description: Rare form affecting nipple skin, often associated with underlying DCIS or invasive cancer

instances.name: Metastatic Breast Cancer
instances.description: Cancer that has spread to distant organs (bones, lungs, liver, brain)

instances.name: Stage 0
instances.description: Non-invasive (DCIS, LCIS, Paget)

instances.name: Stage I
instances.description: Small tumor (<=2cm), little or no lymph node involvement

instances.name: Stage II
instances.description: Larger tumor or limited lymph node spread

instances.name: Stage III
instances.description: Extensive local/regional disease

instances.name: Stage IV
instances.description: Distant metastasis

instances.name: Grade 1
instances.description: Slow-growing, resembles normal cells

instances.name: Grade 2
instances.description: Intermediate growth rate

instances.name: Grade 3
instances.description: Fast-growing, looks very different from normal cells

Symptom.description: Signs and symptoms of breast cancer

instances.name: Bone pain
instances.description: May indicate metastasis

RiskFactor.description: Factors that increase breast cancer risk

ProtectiveFactor.description: Factors that decrease breast cancer risk

GeneticFactor.description: Genes and mutations associated with breast cancer

instances.name: BRCA1
instances.description: Tumor suppressor gene; mutations increase breast/ovarian cancer risk to 45-72%

instances.name: BRCA2
instances.description: Tumor suppressor gene; mutations increase breast cancer risk to 45-69%

instances.name: TP53
instances.description: Rare; increases risk of multiple cancers including breast

instances.name: PALB2
instances.description: Partner of BRCA2; moderate-to-high risk gene

instances.name: ATM
instances.description: Moderate-risk breast cancer gene

instances.name: CHEK2
instances.description: Moderate-risk breast cancer gene

Biomarker.description: Molecular markers used for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection

instances.name: Ki-67
instances.description: Proliferation marker; higher values indicate faster-growing cancer

instances.name: Oncotype DX
instances.description: 21-gene recurrence score; guides chemotherapy decisions in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer

instances.name: MammaPrint
instances.description: 70-gene signature; predicts recurrence risk in early-stage breast cancer

instances.name: PD-L1
instances.description: Immune checkpoint marker; guides immunotherapy decisions in TNBC

DiagnosticTest.description: Tests used to detect and diagnose breast cancer

instances.name: Mammogram
instances.description: X-ray imaging of the breast; primary screening tool

instances.name: Breast Ultrasound
instances.description: Uses sound waves; often used with mammography for dense breasts

instances.name: Breast MRI
instances.description: Magnetic resonance imaging; used for high-risk screening

instances.name: Biopsy
instances.description: Tissue removal for pathological examination

instances.name: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy
instances.description: Checks if cancer has spread to lymph nodes

instances.name: Clinical Breast Exam
instances.description: Physical examination by healthcare provider

instances.name: PET Scan
instances.description: Detects metabolically active cancer cells

instances.name: CT Scan
instances.description: Cross-sectional imaging for staging

instances.name: Bone Scan
instances.description: Checks for bone metastasis

instances.name: Genetic Testing
instances.description: Tests for hereditary cancer gene mutations

instances.name: Immunohistochemistry
instances.description: Tests ER, PR, HER2 status on tissue samples

instances.name: FISH Test
instances.description: Confirms HER2 gene amplification

instances.name: Lumpectomy
instances.description: Removes tumor and margin of normal tissue

instances.name: Mastectomy
instances.description: Removes entire breast

instances.name: Chemotherapy
instances.description: Systemic drug treatment that kills rapidly dividing cells

instances.name: Radiation Therapy
instances.description: High-energy rays to kill cancer cells in a specific area

instances.name: Endocrine Therapy
instances.description: Blocks hormones that fuel HR+ breast cancer growth

instances.name: Targeted Therapy
instances.description: Drugs targeting specific molecular features (e.g., HER2)

instances.name: Immunotherapy
instances.description: Stimulates immune system to attack cancer cells

instances.name: Neoadjuvant Therapy
instances.description: Treatment given before surgery to shrink tumors

instances.name: Adjuvant Therapy
instances.description: Treatment given after surgery to reduce recurrence risk

instances.name: Stem Cell Transplant
instances.description: Replaces blood-forming cells after high-dose chemotherapy

Medication.description: Specific drugs used in breast cancer treatment

SideEffect.description: Adverse effects of breast cancer treatments

instances.name: Local recurrence
instances.description: Cancer returns in the same breast or chest wall

instances.name: Regional recurrence
instances.description: Cancer returns in nearby lymph nodes

instances.name: Distant recurrence
instances.description: Cancer returns in distant organs

Metastasis.description: Spread of cancer to distant sites

instances.name: Bone metastasis
instances.description: Most common site of breast cancer metastasis

instances.name: Mammography screening
instances.description: Recommended annually or biennially starting at age 40-50 depending on guidelines

instances.name: Breast self-exam
instances.description: Self-examination to detect changes

instances.name: Genetic counseling
instances.description: Recommended for high-risk individuals

treats.description: Treatment X is used to treat condition Y

prevents.description: Factor X reduces the likelihood of condition Y developing

increases_risk_of.description: Factor X increases the probability of condition Y
increases_risk_of.example: BRCA1 mutation increases risk of breast cancer

decreases_risk_of.description: Factor X reduces the probability of condition Y
decreases_risk_of.example: Regular exercise decreases risk of breast cancer

detects.description: Test X can identify or diagnose condition Y

has_biomarker.description: Cancer subtype X is characterized by biomarker Y status
has_biomarker.example: HER2-positive breast cancer has_biomarker HER2 overexpression

has_side_effect.description: Treatment X can cause adverse effect Y

contraindicated_for.description: Treatment X should NOT be used for condition/situation Y
contraindicated_for.example: Endocrine therapy is contraindicated for triple-negative breast cancer

associated_with.description: Entity X is statistically or clinically associated with entity Y
associated_with.example: HER2/neu is associated with aggressive tumor behavior

causes.description: Factor X directly causes outcome Y
causes.note: Use sparingly; most cancer relationships are probabilistic, not causal
causes.example: Radiation to chest in adolescence causes increased breast cancer risk

reduces_recurrence_risk.description: Intervention X lowers the chance of cancer returning

improves_survival.description: Intervention X is associated with longer overall or disease-free survival
improves_survival.example: Trastuzumab improves survival in HER2-positive breast cancer

negation.example: Chemotherapy does NOT treat (negated: true) triple-negative breast cancer with endocrine therapy

examples.probable: Exercise likely reduces breast cancer risk
examples.possible: Some studies suggest vitamin D may lower risk
examples.uncertain: The role of diet in breast cancer is unclear

strength.description: How strong the association or effect is

population_scope.description: Which patient population the claim applies to

factual_relations.subject: Pembrolizumab
factual_relations.note: In combination with chemotherapy for early-stage TNBC

factual_relations.subject: Olaparib
factual_relations.note: For BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative early breast cancer

factual_relations.subject: Palbociclib
factual_relations.note: In combination with endocrine therapy for advanced HR+/HER2-

common_misinformation.explanation: No scientific evidence links bra type to breast cancer risk
No conclusive evidence links deodorant use to breast cancer

common_misinformation.claim: If you have no family history, you won't get breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Most breast cancers (~85%) occur in women with no family history. Family history increases risk but is not required.

common_misinformation.claim: A breast cancer diagnosis is a death sentence
common_misinformation.explanation: 5-year relative survival for localized breast cancer is ~99%. Even Stage IV has improving outcomes.

common_misinformation.claim: Chemotherapy won't work for HER2-positive breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Chemotherapy IS used for HER2+ breast cancer, typically in combination with HER2-targeted therapy. Targeted therapy supplements chemo, not replaces it.
Men can get breast cancer too, though it is rare (~1% of cases).

common_misinformation.claim: Mammograms cause breast cancer due to radiation
common_misinformation.explanation: Radiation dose from mammography is very low. Benefits of early detection far outweigh the minimal risk.

common_misinformation.claim: Sugar feeds cancer and you should eliminate it completely
common_misinformation.explanation: All cells use glucose, not just cancer cells. Eliminating sugar doesn't starve cancer. However, excessive sugar intake contributes to obesity, which is a risk factor.

common_misinformation.claim: Natural remedies can cure breast cancer without conventional treatment
common_misinformation.explanation: No natural remedy has been proven to cure breast cancer. Delaying proven treatment can worsen outcomes.

common_misinformation.claim: If your mammogram is normal, you definitely don't have breast cancer
common_misinformation.explanation: Mammograms miss about 1 in 8 breast cancers. Dense breast tissue can obscure tumors. Additional screening may be needed.
